question_text: Was the Workday outage a hack?
answer_text: Reported, on Workday's own account: it says it was not a cyber incident and describes a fault in its own disaster-recovery setup. No independent source confirms that, and Workday has published no root-cause report.
label: Reported
what_would_settle_it: A Workday root-cause report, or an independent statement (CISA, a regulator or an outside investigator) on the cause.

question_text: Were this week's outages, including Workday's, one coordinated attack?
answer_text: Officials say no. A Nov 18 White House release says they see no indication of a coordinated cyberattack and no evidence the incidents are related. It does not name Workday, and the companies gave different causes.
label: Not established
what_would_settle_it: Findings from the companies or an independent investigation tying the incidents together or ruling it out.

question_text: Did the Workday outage lock out millions of employees?
answer_text: Unverified. Workday has said only that some customers were affected. About 11,500 organizations use Workday, but nobody has said how many were hit, and no source gives a count of people.
label: Unverified
what_would_settle_it: Workday or an employer group publishing how many customers and users were affected.

question_text: Did the disaster-recovery site connect to production hours before the outage, and was only one environment involved first?
answer_text: Rumor. The claim comes from forum posts repeated by a vendor blog that calls them unverified. Workday's notice gives no such timeline.
label: Rumor
what_would_settle_it: A Workday root-cause report with a timeline.
